bull_bear.body: Prioritize music content (70%+ of capex); reinvest in artist management & live events; maintain net cash position; no dividends or buybacks mentioned; future AI licensing deals to be opportunistic, not capex-heavy
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Punjabi market execution risk; festival breakeven delayed beyond FY28; AI regulatory uncertainty; subscription growth slower than expected; content ROI misjudgment on new releases
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, disciplined, long-term oriented; emphatic on economic rigor (no vanity buys), proud of operational efficiency (Pocket Aces breakeven), bullish on India’s subscription runway, dismissive of AI-generated content threat, focused on institutionalizing IP as infrastructure
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Pocket Aces’ digital muscle is now a cost-saving engine for music marketing, not just a content creator; UN40’s non-music elements (comedy, games) are strategic differentiators reducing artist dependency; Bhansali deal effectively locks in premium Hindi film music without upfront licensing fees; Saregama’s non-digital revenue (physical, radio, sync) remains #1 in India despite digital focus
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Dividend per share has been raised over the cycle: INR 3.0 (FY22), 3.0 (FY23), 4.0 (FY24), 4.5 (FY25), 4.5 (FY26); dividend paid in FY26 was INR 868 Mn.
- The financial-charts slide shows Net Debt to Equity Ratio as NIL; current borrowings are footnoted as 'temporary use of WC limits'.
- Since FY22, INR 7,500 Mn of fresh fund raise through QIP has been added to shareholders' equity.
- Net worth stood at INR 17,547 Mn as at 30-Jun-26 versus INR 16,927 Mn as at 31-Mar-26; the company also holds investments in bank FDs (maturity over 3 months) and mutual funds of INR 2,030 Mn (FY26: INR 1,889 Mn) outside reported cash.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Music vertical: INR 814cr revenue (+17% YoY), EBITDA INR 517cr (+22% YoY), net margin INR 377cr (+28% YoY); Live events: INR 62cr revenue (excl. FY25 one-off Diljit tour), UN40 festival loss in Q4 due to inaugural spend; Video: INR 108cr (-44% YoY) due to deliberate wind-down of Yoodlee film production; Artist management: 300+ artists, 400M+ digital followers; Retail (Carvaan): Stable, integrated with live events; Bhansali: Strategic minority stake, exclusive access to future film music via performance-linked valuation
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Stated strategy on the cover slide: 'OWN THE IP IN PERPETUITY. THEN COMPOUND IT ACROSS EVERY FORMAT THAT INDIA'S DIGITAL BOOM OPENS UP.'
- Two moats claimed: an owned catalogue of 1,80,000+ songs (master and underlying works, in perpetuity, global territory) and a large owned audience of 680 Mn+ subscribers and followers across the portfolio.
- Owned content beyond music: 70+ films, 55+ digital series, 10K+ hours of TV, across 14+ Indian languages.
- Deck frames revenue as 'Diversified Across Segments, Partners and Revenue Sources - No Single Point of Dependence', spanning platform (Spotify, YouTube, Netflix, JioHotstar, Sun TV, Doordarshan, Instagram), brand (Myntra, Indriya, Unilever, KFC, Hero) and customer (Amazon, Vijay Sales, BookMyShow, District, PVR).
- The company describes an 'Entertainment Flywheel framework' in which the integrated ecosystem across music, video, live events and artiste management maximises the value of its intellectual property.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Group] Saregama is part of the RP-Sanjiv Goenka (RPSG) Group, whose businesses span power and energy, carbon black, retail, IT enabled services, FMCG, media and entertainment, and agriculture.
- [Demerger] FY23 numbers are re-stated, as applicable, post the impact of the demerger; the FY26 cash flow also shows INR 36 Mn 'Transferred pursuant to Demerger/ Finnet'.
- [Base effect] Live events is described as lumpy in nature, with FY25 carrying a one-off Diljit Dosanjh India tour - the reason FY26 headline revenue (INR 9,846 Mn) is below FY25 (INR 11,713 Mn) while the deck flags revenue up excluding the one-off live-events base.
- [Regulation] An exceptional item of INR (85) Mn in FY26 is attributed to the impact of the new labour code.
- [Non-GAAP] The disclaimer states EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA Margin, PAT Margin, Debt to Equity, and ROE are non-GAAP measures not defined under Ind AS and may not be comparable to similarly titled measures of other companies.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin expansion driven by: (1) removal of Wynk revenue from denominator; (2) higher mix of paid subscription revenue; (3) lower incremental marketing cost via Pocket Aces digital footprint; (4) amortization of prior-year hits (Stree 2, Amaran) benefiting FY26; (5) no new content over-investment in FY26 (INR 235cr vs planned) due to film delays
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: 20-23% CAGR for music vertical (licensing + artist mgmt + retail); margin: 60-65% EBITDA margin for music vertical; order inflow: N/A; capex/commissioning: FY27 content spend INR 300-350cr; UN40 festival to break even by FY28; Carvaan Live concerts scaling; Bhansali deal locks in A/B+ film music for 24-30 months
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Punjabi music market entry (new model: combined recorded + live deals); US diaspora tours (Ilaiyaraaja, Sudesh Bhosle); AI licensing partnerships (future monetization); UN40 festival expansion (annual); short-form video monetization via Pocket Aces
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Saregama delivered record EBITDA and PAT driven by music vertical growth post-Airtel Wynk exit, with strategic content spend discipline and new monetization levers like UN40 festival and Bhansali partnership creating durable upside; the shift from vanity-driven acquisitions to 5-year payback discipline and AI efficiency gains positions it as India’s dominant music IP infrastructure play.

meta.thesis: Saregama delivered record EBITDA and PAT driven by music vertical growth post-Airtel Wynk exit, with strategic content spend discipline and new monetization levers like UN40 festival and Bhansali partnership creating durable upside; the shift from vanity-driven acquisitions to 5-year payback discipline and AI efficiency gains positions it as India’s dominant music IP infrastructure play.
